subject: Conditional reserve structure and GPU-price surge contingency
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Adams <rachel.adams@aureliahealth.com>; Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 15:32:00 -0700
Subject: Conditional reserve structure and GPU-price surge contingency

Rachel — attaching a refreshed reserve proposal that mirrors the sizing we discussed on the call but includes an explicit contingency for GPU market volatility. Key points up front: 

- Proposed reserved capacity: 1200 reserved GPU-hours / month (Aurora-XL equivalent) with 12-month tenor.
- Base commercial: standard reserved discount (20%) for the committed volume.
- Contingency mechanism: if underlying GPU spot index increases >12% vs baseline, we trigger an automatic protection schedule (either temporary surcharge or credit from our market buffer pool).

Why this helps Aurelia: it keeps your run-rate predictable while giving both sides a clear, measurable trigger if the market moves. From our side, the contingency preserves unit economics without blocking a deal.

Please find attached: reserve_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal + mutually actionable milestones). Specific asks from your procurement team: confirmation of billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether a fixed-price escrow is required.

Next steps (suggested):
1) You confirm timing and any hard floor you need for discounts by EOD Mon 5/7.
2) We get finance to sign off on the contingency ladder (I’m looping Marcus and Karthik for that).
3) DocuSign-ready SOW once terms agreed.

Happy to jump on a 15-min call if procurement wants to walk through the trigger math.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: reserve_proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
From: Rachel Adams <rachel.adams@aureliahealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 04 May 2028 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional reserve structure and GPU-price surge contingency

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the clear summary and the proposal. A couple of quick clarifications from procurement: 

- We need a firm floor on discounts for internal approval; 20% is in the ballpark but I need confirmation there is no unilateral step-down within the first 6 months.
- If you suggest a surcharge option when the index moves, we need a capped exposure per month and an escalation path to our legal/finance if trigger events persist.
- Procurement timeline: we need signed terms by 5/22 to align with our budget cycle.

Can Marcus or Karthik confirm the maximum monthly exposure Aurelia would see under the contingency? If you can provide a capped-credit alternative (company-provided credit pool), that would be ideal for our CFO.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Adams
Head of Platform Procurement | Aurelia Health
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 05 May 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional reserve structure and GPU-price surge contingency — internal ask

Looping necessary internal stakeholders. Rachel’s ask is reasonable: she wants a firm discount floor and a capped exposure if we use a surcharge. Proposed internal approach: 

- Offer: base 20% reserved discount guaranteed for first 6 months. For months 7–12, discount remains at 20% unless index >12% at which point we move to a dynamic protection ladder.
- Protection ladder (example):
  * Index increase 12–20%: temporary surcharge applied to overage portion only, capped at 8% of monthly invoice;
  * Index increase >20%: trigger access to our market buffer credit pool (capped credit of $50k/month for first 3 months) while we reprice long-term.

- Maximum customer exposure under surcharge path: capped at 8% of monthly invoice. If we hit the buffer credit, Aurelia receives credit against invoice instead of surcharge.

Action items for approvals: 
- Finance (Kimberly): confirm credit-pool allocation and whether $50k/month is acceptable as an interim.
- Legal (Ben): quick review of surcharge wording and whether we require any additional indemnities.
- Solutions (Karthik): confirm that the sizing (1200 GPU-hrs) and burst profile in the proposal is operationally sound.

I’ve attached a simple sensitivity model (pricing_sensitivity_model.xlsx) that maps invoice outcomes under different index moves. If finance signs off on the $50k buffer and legal clears the contract language, Stephanie can present the structure to Aurelia next week and push for 5/22 signature.

Marcus Lin
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing_sensitivity_model.xlsx]
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 May 2028 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Conditional reserve structure and GPU-price surge contingency — finance approval

Thanks for the clear breakdown — reviewed the attached sensitivity model. Finance is comfortable with the proposed construct with the following guardrails: 

- Approve base 20% discount guaranteed for months 1–6.
- Approve temporary surcharge path capped at 8% of monthly invoice when index moves 12–20%.
- Approve one-time access to the market buffer credit pool (cap $50k/month) for up to 3 consecutive months if index >20%.
- Exception path: discounts >22% or buffer credit >$50k/month require VP Sales sign-off (Marcus to escalate if needed).

Please have Legal (Ben) confirm the contract language includes: defined index, measurement window (30-day rolling), and automatic notification cadence to Aurelia and Redwood when triggers occur. Once Ben confirms, Stephanie should send the DocuSign-ready SOW. I’ve pre-approved the DocuSign template for this deal; link below. 

DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/en/embeddedSigning?docId=abcd-1234-aur-commit

Kimberly Park
Head of Finance, Commercial | Redwood Inference
